messages:
Nina Park: Dropping a quick thread with two variants for the Profile settings form. Variant 1 = "progressive inline" (short inline messages + subtle red ring). Variant 2 = "summary reveal" (tiny inline dots + a collapsed error panel that expands on submit). Also prototyped a lightweight destructive confirm that uses a checkbox + rationale field instead of typed-confirm. Looking for accessibility, copy and density feedback. Owen Li: Quick take: progressive inline feels immediate for single edits. summary reveal is cleaner for long multi-section forms. Concern: collapsed panel could be overlooked on mobile if it's low in the view. Carlos M.: For list/table UIs the inline copy is heavy. I like the idea of tiny error dots + a reveal panel when errors > 1. For bulk failures show per-row microstates and open the panel automatically when many failures occur. Rina Ahmed: A11y notes: collapsed error panel must be in an assertive live region and focus should shift to it when opened by submit failure. Example pattern suggestion: ```
Save blocked 1 errors. Expand to review.
``` Nina Park: Copy idea for panel header: "Save blocked 1 issues. Expand to see fixes." Short and scannable. Also thoughts on required marker treatments: current comps show a small badge that reads "Required" vs an asterisk. Which do we pick? Owen Li: I prefer the explicit badge for critical fields (billing/org name). Asterisk alone is subtle and non-descriptive. Badge is ok on desktop; on mobile collapse to an icon but ensure aria-required remains. Carlos M.: Badge helps discovery but adds visual weight. Maybe show badge on first interaction or hover, keep asterisk by default. Whatever we choose, also set `aria-required` and include the word "(required)" in the label for screen readers. Rina Ahmed: Also ensure invalid inputs get `aria-invalid=\"true\"` and their messages referenced with `aria-describedby`. When the panel opens, focus it and programmatically focus the first invalid control as a second step. Nina Park: Confirm pattern: checkbox + rationale vs typed-confirm. Prototype uses a checkbox labeled "I understand this will permanently remove X" + small freeform reason. I thought this is less painful for admins than typing a name. Safety tradeoffs? Owen Li: Checkbox is faster but easier to bypass. For org-level irreversible deletes prefer typed-confirm or exact-name. Checkbox + reason is fine for dataset-level deletions where audits exist. Consider adding a cooldown or an admin permission gate for repeated deletes. Carlos M.: Agree. Also if using checkbox, require it to be keyboard-focusable and include clear aria instructions. For high-risk actions prefer typed-confirm. For medium risk checkbox + reason + a short delay works. DesignBot: Quick accessibility scan: Variant 1 inline helper contrast = 3.5:1 (recommend >=4.5:1). Variant 2 collapsed panel missing `aria-label` and no programmatic focus on open. Checkbox confirm flow missing an accessible description for screen readers. Recommendations: increase helper contrast or weight; add `aria-label=\"Form errors\"` to the panel and call `.focus()` on reveal; ensure confirm checkbox has `aria-describedby` pointing to the rationale instructions. Also add `aria-invalid` on invalid inputs. Nina Park: Great — actionable list: 1) bump inline helper contrast >=4.5:1 or use stronger weight; 2) add assertive live region + `aria-label` for the reveal panel and move focus into it on submit fail; 3) ensure first invalid field is focused after panel reveal; 4) reserve typed-confirm/exact-name for irreversible org deletes; allow checkbox+reason for medium-risk deletes but include an admin cooldown/audit trail; 5) include explicit "Required" badge for critical fields (collapse on mobile but keep `aria-required`). I'll update the comps and post links. Tagging @Carlos to draft short reason microcopy for the checkbox flow. Thanks all :sparkles:
